youtube.title: Kaliningrad: Russia's Exclave Ringed by NATO, German Until 1945
youtube.description:
Kaliningrad is a Russian region of about a million people that touches no other Russian land. Until 1945 its capital was the German city of Königsberg. How did Russia come to hold it, why can't Russia reach it overland, and why do NATO planners watch a 65 km strip of farmland beside it?

This episode measures the region on the map: its borders, its port, its rail line through Lithuania and its sea route from St Petersburg. It then follows how those lines were drawn in 1758, 1945 and 1991, sets out Russia's case and Lithuania's case in the 2022 transit dispute, and maps three paths the region could take.

sources.claim: Kaliningrad Oblast covers 15,125 square kilometres
sources.source: Rosstat, Regions of Russia statistical yearbook, 2023

sources.claim: Lithuania stopped rail transit of EU-sanctioned goods to Kaliningrad on 18 June 2022, starting with steel and other ferrous metals
sources.source: Reuters, 18-20 June 2022; Lithuanian Railways notice, 17 June 2022

sources.claim: The Suwałki gap is about 65 km wide
sources.source: CEPA, 'Securing the Suwałki Corridor', Hodges et al., July 2018

sources.claim: NATO has 32 member countries
sources.source: NATO, Sweden's accession, 7 March 2024

sources.claim: Königsberg was German until 1945; renamed Kaliningrad on 4 July 1946
sources.source: Decree of the Presidium of the Supreme Soviet of the USSR, 4 July 1946

sources.claim: Russian troops entered Königsberg in January 1758
sources.source: Franz Szabo, 'The Seven Years War in Europe 1756-1763', 2008

sources.claim: Border with Poland 209 km; border with Lithuania 261 km; Polish-Lithuanian border 104 km
sources.source: CIA World Factbook, Lithuania and Poland entries, 2024

sources.claim: Moscow is about 1,090 km from Kaliningrad in a straight line
sources.source: Great-circle distance between city centres (54.71N 20.45E to 55.76N 37.62E)

sources.claim: About 1.03 million people live in the region, nearly half in the city of Kaliningrad
sources.source: Rosstat, All-Russian Population Census 2021: region 1,029,966, city 489,359

sources.claim: The Kaliningrad sea canal is 43 km long
sources.source: Kaliningrad Sea Port authority; canal opened 1901

sources.claim: Baltiysk is the main base of the Baltic Fleet and Russia's westernmost naval port
sources.source: Russian Ministry of Defence, Baltic Fleet page, 2024

sources.claim: The Strait of Baltiysk is the only natural exit of the Vistula Lagoon, shared by Russia and Poland
sources.source: Polish Maritime Office in Gdynia, Vistula Spit project documentation, 2022

sources.claim: The Curonian Spit is 98 km long and shared by Russia and Lithuania
sources.source: UNESCO World Heritage List, Curonian Spit, inscribed 2000

sources.claim: The region holds about 90% of the world's amber reserves
sources.source: Kaliningrad Amber Combine (Rostec), company statement, 2021

sources.claim: Cargo ferries run between Ust-Luga and Baltiysk
sources.source: Russian Ministry of Transport, Kaliningrad ferry line reports, 2022-2023

sources.claim: Sweden joined NATO in March 2024; Finland in April 2023
sources.source: NATO, 7 March 2024 and 4 April 2023

sources.claim: The Baltic states left the Russian-run BRELL grid on 8 February 2025 and joined the continental European grid on 9 February
sources.source: ENTSO-E and Litgrid statements, 8-9 February 2025

sources.claim: The Suwałki gap is the only land link between the Baltic states and the rest of NATO
sources.source: CEPA, 'Securing the Suwałki Corridor', July 2018

sources.claim: Teutonic Knights founded Königsberg in 1255, by tradition named after King Ottokar II of Bohemia
sources.source: Andreas Kossert, 'Ostpreussen: Geschichte und Mythos', 2005

sources.claim: Königsberg became capital of the Duchy of Prussia in 1525; Frederick I was crowned there on 18 January 1701
sources.source: Christopher Clark, 'Iron Kingdom', 2006

sources.claim: East Prussia's estates swore allegiance to Empress Elizabeth during the occupation of 1758-1762
sources.source: Christopher Clark, 'Iron Kingdom', 2006

sources.claim: Kant petitioned Empress Elizabeth for a professorship in December 1758 and was not appointed
sources.source: Manfred Kuehn, 'Kant: A Biography', 2001

sources.claim: Peter III made peace with Prussia in 1762 and returned East Prussia
sources.source: Treaty of Saint Petersburg, 5 May 1762; Szabo, 2008

sources.claim: The Treaty of Versailles gave Poland a corridor to the sea, separating East Prussia from Germany
sources.source: Treaty of Versailles, signed 28 June 1919, in force 10 January 1920

sources.claim: Germans reached East Prussia by sea or sealed transit trains across Poland
sources.source: Paris Transit Agreement between Germany and Poland, 21 April 1921

sources.claim: British bombers destroyed much of the old city in August 1944
sources.source: RAF Bomber Command campaign records, raids of 26-27 and 29-30 August 1944

sources.claim: The German garrison surrendered to the Soviet army on 9 April 1945
sources.source: Kossert, 2005; Soviet Information Bureau communiqué, 9-10 April 1945

sources.claim: At Potsdam the Allies agreed 'in principle' to transfer Königsberg and the area adjacent to the Soviet Union, pending a peace settlement
sources.source: Protocol of the Proceedings of the Berlin (Potsdam) Conference, 1 August 1945, Section VI

sources.claim: East Prussia was divided between the Soviet Union and Poland; the Memel area went to Soviet Lithuania
sources.source: Potsdam Protocol, 1945; Kossert, 2005

sources.claim: Mikhail Kalinin died on 3 June 1946
sources.source: Great Soviet Encyclopedia, 3rd edition

sources.claim: The remaining German residents were deported to Germany in 1947-1948
sources.source: Per Brodersen, 'Die Stadt im Westen', 2008

sources.claim: Germany renounced all territorial claims against other states
sources.source: Treaty on the Final Settlement with Respect to Germany, 12 September 1990, Article 1(3)

sources.claim: Lithuania declared independence on 11 March 1990; the USSR recognised it on 6 September 1991
sources.source: Act of the Re-Establishment of the State of Lithuania, 11 March 1990; USSR State Council resolution, 6 September 1991

sources.claim: Poland joined NATO in 1999, Lithuania in 2004; both joined the EU in 2004
sources.source: NATO, 12 March 1999 and 29 March 2004; EU enlargement, 1 May 2004

sources.claim: In 2002 Russia and the EU agreed simplified transit across Lithuania
sources.source: Joint Statement of the EU and the Russian Federation on Transit between the Kaliningrad Region and the Rest of the Russian Federation, 11 November 2002

sources.claim: Vladimir Shamanov said Iskander missiles were deployed in the Kaliningrad region
sources.source: Interfax, 5 February 2018

sources.claim: Russia gives the Iskander's range as up to 500 km
sources.source: Russian Ministry of Defence, Iskander-M description

sources.claim: Warsaw is about 280 km from Kaliningrad
sources.source: Great-circle distance between city centres

sources.claim: At the 2016 Warsaw summit NATO agreed to station multinational battlegroups in Poland, Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania
sources.source: NATO Warsaw Summit Communiqué, 9 July 2016

sources.claim: Germany commissioned a brigade in Lithuania in April 2025, its first permanent unit stationed abroad since the Second World War
sources.source: Bundeswehr, Panzerbrigade 45 commissioning, 1 April 2025

sources.claim: Germany plans about 4,800 soldiers in the brigade by 2027
sources.source: German Federal Ministry of Defence, 2024

sources.claim: Governor Anton Alikhanov said 40-50% of the region's imports were affected
sources.source: Reuters, 20 June 2022

sources.claim: Russia's Foreign Ministry called the restrictions a breach of the 2002 transit arrangements and demanded they be lifted
sources.source: Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs statement, 20 June 2022

sources.claim: The Kremlin said its deployments in Kaliningrad respond to NATO activity near Russia's borders
sources.source: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov, reported by Reuters, October 2016

sources.claim: Lithuania said it was applying EU sanctions, not its own, and passenger traffic continued
sources.source: Lithuanian Foreign Minister Gabrielius Landsbergis, Reuters, 20 June 2022

sources.claim: The European Commission said sanctioned goods could transit by rail but not road; military goods not at all
sources.source: European Commission, guidance on transit to Kaliningrad, 13 July 2022

sources.claim: Poland opened a canal about 1.3 km long through the Vistula Spit on 17 September 2022
sources.source: Polish Ministry of Infrastructure, 17 September 2022

sources.claim: A Polish naming commission recommended the name Królewiec in May 2023
sources.source: Commission for the Standardisation of Geographical Names outside Poland, 9 May 2023

sources.claim: Poland's defence spending rose from 1.85% of GDP in 2014 to 4.12% in 2024 and an estimated 4.48% in 2025
sources.source: NATO, Defence Expenditure of NATO Countries (2014-2025), June 2025

sources.claim: Poland's East Shield programme, about 10 billion zloty, to be completed by 2028
sources.source: Polish Prime Minister's Office, 18 May 2024

sources.claim: Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania agreed a Baltic Defence Line in January 2024
sources.source: Joint statement of the Baltic defence ministers, 19 January 2024

sources.claim: In a 2016 RAND wargame Russian forces reached the outskirts of Tallinn or Riga in 60 hours at most
sources.source: RAND, Shlapak and Johnson, 'Reinforcing Deterrence on NATO's Eastern Flank', 2016

sources.claim: Putin said Russia has no interest in Poland, Latvia or anywhere else
sources.source: Vladimir Putin, interview with Tucker Carlson, published 8 February 2024

sources.claim: Local border traffic between Kaliningrad and a Polish zone including Gdańsk ran from July 2012; Poland suspended it on 4 July 2016
sources.source: Poland-Russia local border traffic agreement, 14 December 2011, in force 27 July 2012; Polish Ministry of Interior, 4 July 2016

sources.claim: The Bosporus is about 700 m wide at its narrowest; the 1936 Montreux Convention lets Turkey regulate warship passage
sources.source: Montreux Convention Regarding the Regime of the Straits, 20 July 1936; Turkish Hydrography Office
